summary: T. V. Ramachandra Dikshitar was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He served as Principal of Madras Sanskrit College (attested 1938) and as Professor of Advaita Vedanta at Banaras Hindu University (attested 1946).

T. V. Vasudeva works in Indology and philosophy and taught S. N. Krishna. He served on the Editorial Committee (attested 2001) and later as Deputy Director (attested 2026) at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute.

T. V. Venkatachala Sastry is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Mysore under teachers including K. V. Puttappa, D. L. Narasimhachar, and Harogadde Manappa Nayak, later serving there as lecturer and Professor (1984–1994).
T. Venkatacharya was an Indology scholar who held positions at the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East (attested 1971) and as Professor at the University of Toronto (attested 1971–1979).

T. W. Rhys Davids (1843–1922) worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics, earning his Ph.D. at the University of Breslau under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler. He founded the Pali Text Society and held professorships at the University of London and University of Manchester.
T. Y. Lee is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at the Mangala Vihara Buddhist Temple and the Buddhist and Pali College of Singapore.

Tadao Yoshikawa is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied at Kyoto University. His academic posts include assistant professor at Kyoto University, professor at Ryukoku University (2002), and director of the International Research Institute for Zen Buddhism (c. 2003–2011).

Tadashi Inoue (1929–2014) was a historian and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Kyoto National Museum, Iida City Museum, and professorships at Nara University, Bukkyo University, and Kyoto University of the Arts.

Tadashi Sekino (1868–1935) was a scholar of history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (c. 1892–1895) and later served there as professor emeritus (c. 1929–1935).

Tadashi Tani is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed doctoral studies at Waseda University, studied under Yuichi Kajiyama at Kyoto University, and served as professor at the National Institute of Technology, Kochi College (attested 1996–2000).
Tadashi Toda is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under Keiki Higashimoto and Kogen Mizuno.

Tadeusz Skorupski is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who earned his Ph.D. from the University of London in 1978. He served as Professor and Reader in the Department of the Study of Religions at SOAS University of London.
Tai-shing Wut is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned a Ph.D. at the University of Hong Kong under the supervision of Ming-Wood Liu (attested 1998).
Taido Kitamura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He served as an assistant professor (attested 1980) and held a post at Shuchiin University (attested 1994–1999).

Taigen Dan Leighton is a Buddhist studies and Japanology scholar who earned degrees from Columbia University and the Graduate Theological Union. He has taught at the Institute of Buddhist Studies, Loyola University Chicago, and several other institutions.

Taijun Inokuchi is a scholar of Buddhist and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He served as a lecturer and committee member at Ryukoku University (attested 1963–1987) and as representative of The Society for the History of Buddhism (attested 1988).

Taiken Kimura (1881–1930) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo under Junjirō Takakusu and Tetsujiro Inoue, later becoming a professor of Indian philosophy at the University of Tokyo in 1912.

Taiken Kyuma is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Vienna in 1999 and served as Associate Professor at Mie University (attested 2002–2008).
Taiken Tanaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Hiroshima University. He served as an assistant professor at Aichi Gakuin University (attested 1991).
Taiki Mibu is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Ph.D. at Ryukoku University by 2016 and served there as a part-time lecturer (attested 2015).
